paper_title: Hitting Geodesic Intervals in Structurally Restricted Graphs
classifications: Theory of computation → Parameterized complexity and exact algorithms
statement: Question: Is there Z ⊆ V with |Z| ≤ p such that each connected component C of G − Z contains at most q terminal vertices (i.e., |V (C) ∩ R| ≤ q)?
context: Input: A graph G = (V, E), a set of terminal vertices R ⊆ V , and integers p and q. Question: Is there Z ⊆ V with |Z| ≤ p such that each connected component C of G − Z contains at most q terminal vertices (i.e., |V (C) ∩ R| ≤ q)? Note that, as we discussed in the last paragraph of Section 4.2.2, the graph minor theorem gives a nonuniform fixed-parameter algorithm parameterized by p + q for this problem, while we are looking for a uniform one.
